In mathematics, a '''twisted sheaf'''  is a variant of a [[coherent sheaf]]. Precisely, it is specified by: an [[open covering]] in the [[étale topology]] ''U''<sub>''i''</sub>, coherent sheaves ''F''<sub>''i''</sub> over ''U''<sub>''i''</sub>, a [[Čech cohomology|Čech 2-cocycle]] ''θ'' for <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math> on the covering ''U''<sub>''i''</sub> as well as the isomorphisms
:<math>g_{ij}: F_j|_{U_{ij}} \overset{\sim}\to F_i|_{U_{ij}} </math>
satisfying
*<math>g_{ii} = \operatorname{id}_{F_i}</math>,
*<math>g_{ij} = g_{ji}^{-1},</math>
*<math>g_{ij} \circ g_{jk} \circ g_{ki} = \theta_{ijk} \operatorname{id}_{F_i}.</math>

The notion of twisted sheaves was introduced by [[Jean Giraud (mathematician)|Jean Giraud]]. The above definition due to Căldăraru is down-to-earth but is equivalent to a more sophisticated definition in terms of [[gerbe]]; see § 2.1.3 of {{harv|Lieblich|2007}}.
